title: Data and reports
covers: Analyses, KPI reports, the numbers in dashboards, datasets, pipeline outputs and predictions someone acts on.

stakeholders.who: The person who acts on the numbers (owner, manager or client)
cares_about: knowing how sure the result is
would_notice: a bar chart whose axis does not start at zero
a headline number with no period or 'as of' date
a 0 where there simply was no data

stakeholders.who: A second analyst who checks the method
cares_about: recomputing one figure and getting the same result
would_notice: a join that counts rows twice
rows dropped silently because of empty values
a different number on a rerun

stakeholders.who: The people whose data is in the dataset
cares_about: their personal data kept out of view
would_notice: names, e-mail addresses or phone numbers in a chart, export, log or browser bundle

first_ten_seconds: Read the top of the report: is the main finding stated in one plain sentence?
Does the headline number say its period, its unit and how fresh the data is?
Look at the first chart: does its axis start where it should, with units and a legend?

checks.claim: Figures come from the real data source, not sample or synthetic data, and one headline figure was recomputed independently.
checks.how_to_inspect: Name the source table or file and its extraction time; recompute one headline figure with a separate query or by hand.
checks.evidence_required: The source, the recompute query and both results.

source.quote: must prove real fixtures were used

checks.claim: Aggregations are correct: no rows dropped by empty values, no double counting from joins, and every filter stated.
checks.how_to_inspect: Compare row counts before and after each join and filter, and count empty values in the grouped columns.

checks.claim: Every figure states its period and timezone, and period boundaries are right (week start, month end, daylight-saving change).
checks.how_to_inspect: Check that a record near midnight and one near a month boundary land in the right bucket.
checks.evidence_required: The boundary records and where they landed.

checks.claim: Estimates and predictions carry a confidence, range or risk label and the sample size; nothing is stated as certain.
checks.how_to_inspect: Read every predicted or estimated number in the output and check it has its label and its sample size.
checks.evidence_required: A sample of outputs with their labels (N/A when nothing is estimated).

source.quote: Every output carries a confidence/risk label.

checks.claim: Charts do not mislead: bar axes start at zero, axes and units are labelled, the legend matches the colours, and text is readable at the size shown.
checks.how_to_inspect: Look at each chart at its real display size and check axis start, labels, units and legend.
checks.evidence_required: A screenshot of each chart with notes.

source.rationale: A truncated axis or an unlabeled unit changes the decision of the person who acts on the chart.

checks.claim: Missing or failed data shows an empty or error state, never a zero or a flat line that looks like a real value.
checks.how_to_inspect: Point the view or report at an empty period and at a failing source and screenshot both.

checks.claim: The report says how fresh its data is ('as of' time) and flags data that is late or suspiciously small.
checks.how_to_inspect: Find the 'as of' line and check what happens when the latest load is missing or has far fewer rows than usual.
checks.evidence_required: The 'as of' line and the late or low-volume behaviour.

checks.claim: The main finding and what it means come first, in one or two plain sentences, before tables and charts.
checks.how_to_inspect: Read only the first paragraph and check that it states the finding and its consequence.

source.rationale: Decision makers read the top of a report; a finding buried further down is a finding they miss.

checks.claim: Running the pipeline or report again gives the same numbers and no duplicate rows.
checks.how_to_inspect: Run it twice on the same input and compare totals and row counts.
checks.evidence_required: Both runs' totals and row counts.

source.quote: a rerun proven to produce no duplicates (idempotency evidence)

checks.claim: Data-source quality and every assumption (exclusions, imputations, definitions) are written down where the reader can find them.
checks.how_to_inspect: List the choices made while preparing the data and check each one appears in the report or its notes.

source.quote: Verify data-source quality; track all assumptions.

checks.claim: No personal data appears in charts, exports, logs, git or the browser bundle unless the purpose needs it, and then masked or scoped.
checks.how_to_inspect: Search outputs, logs and the built bundle for e-mail addresses, phone numbers and name columns.
checks.evidence_required: The search command and its output (zero hits, or each hit fixed).

source.quote: PII classified, masked/scoped, and absent from logs and git

checks.claim: Numbers are formatted for reading: thousands separators, consistent decimals, units and currency, and percent kept apart from percentage points.
checks.how_to_inspect: Scan every table and label for separators, decimals, units and the percent wording.

common_sloppy_defects.symptom: a dip to 0 on the day the import failed
a bar chart starting at 90 that makes a 2 percent change look like a doubling
'Revenue: 12,400' with no month, currency or 'as of' time
order totals higher than the shop's own figure after joining line items
'Team A will win' with no probability or sample size
